title: LOFT: Low-Rank Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Task-Aware Support Selection
claim: Many adaptation methods are special cases of one subspace-rotation form, differing only in how the adapted subspace is chosen.
layout: 2 regions: left weight-matrix schematic with formula, right three geometric panels
description: The left side has a 'Unified Framework' banner. Under it is a box for the pretrained weight W0 (d_out by d_in). A arrow leads to a slanted plane of small arrows labeled 'selected support P_r ⊂ R^d_in (r-dimensional)'. Below is the update equation W+ = W0(I − PrᵀPr) + W0 Prᵀ Tr Pr, with legend chips for 'unchanged complement' (gray) and 'adapted subspace' (blue). The right side is titled 'Representative Choices of Pr' and has three panels with labeled headers: coordinate/structured subspace, principal subspace of W, and gradient-informed subspace. Each panel shows 2-D or 3-D axes with blue arrows (pretrained directions) rotated by angles θ into orange arrows (adapted directions) inside a shaded region: a square, an ellipse, and an orange cone for the task gradient. Captions below link each choice to GOFT-style or PSOFT-type methods.
caption: LOFT as right-subspace adaptation. Left: the transform Tr acts only on the selected right support Pr; the orthogonal complement is unchanged. Right: coordinate, principal and gradient- informed supports instantiate different orthogonal PEFT regimes within one right-multiplicative form.
abstract: Orthogonal parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapts pretrained weights through structure-preserving multiplicative transformations, but existing methods often conflate two distinct design choices: the subspace in which adaptation occurs and the transformation applied within that subspace. This paper introduces LOFT, a low-rank orthogonal fine-tuning framework that explicitly separates these two components. By viewing orthogonal adaptation as a multiplicative subspace rotation, LOFT provides a unified formulation that recovers the multiplicative core of representative orthogonal PEFT methods, including coordinate-, butterfly-, Householder- (with a learnable support) and principal-subspace-based variants (up to scaling and relaxation). More importantly, this perspective exposes support selection as a central design axis rather than a byproduct of a particular parameterization. We develop a first-order analysis showing that useful adaptation supports should be informed by the downstream training signal, motivating practical task-aware support selection strategies. Across language understanding, visual transfer, mathematical reasoning, and multilingual out-of-distribution adaptation, LOFT with task-aware supports improves performance at matched trainable-parameter and transform settings under a shared protocol. This suggests that, under a fixed transform and budget, the choice of support affects performance, making systematic support selection an important direction for improving orthogonal PEFT.
